# Introduction

**mdBook** is a command line tool to create books with Markdown.
It is ideal for creating product or API documentation, tutorials, course materials or anything that requires a clean,
easily navigable and customizable presentation.

* Lightweight [Markdown] syntax helps you focus more on your content
* Integrated [search] support
* Color [syntax highlighting] for code blocks for many different languages
* [Theme] files allow customizing the formatting of the output
* [Preprocessors] can provide extensions for custom syntax and modifying content
* [Backends] can render the output to multiple formats
* Written in [Rust] for speed, safety, and simplicity
* Automated testing of [Rust code samples]

This guide is an example of what mdBook produces.
mdBook is used by the Rust programming language project, and [The Rust Programming Language][trpl] book is another fine example of mdBook in action.

# Running `mdbook` in Continuous Integration

There are a variety of services such as [GitHub Actions] or [GitLab CI/CD] which can be used to test and deploy your book automatically.

The following provides some general guidelines on how to configure your service to run mdBook.
Specific recipes can be found at the [Automated Deployment] wiki page.

[GitHub Actions]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions
[GitLab CI/CD]: https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/
[Automated Deployment]: https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook/wiki/Automated-Deployment

## Installing mdBook

There are several different strategies for installing mdBook.
The particular method depends on your needs and preferences.

### Pre-compiled binaries

Perhaps the easiest method is to use the pre-compiled binaries found on the [GitHub Releases page][releases].
A simple approach would be to use the popular `curl` CLI tool to download the executable:

```sh
mkdir bin
curl -sSL https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook/releases/download/v0.4.52/mdbook-v0.4.52-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz | tar -xz --directory=bin
bin/mdbook build
```

Some considerations for this approach:

* This is relatively fast, and does not necessarily require dealing with caching.
* This does not require installing Rust.
* Specifyi

**non-breaking** version of mdBook.
For example:

```sh
cargo install mdbook --no-default-features --features search --vers "^0.4" --locked
```

This includes several recommended options:

* `--no-default-features` --- Disables features like the HTTP server used by `mdbook serve` that is likely not needed on CI.
  This will speed up the build time significantly.
* `--features search` --- Disabling default features means you should then manually enable features that you want, such as the built-in [search] capability.
* `--vers "^0.4"` --- This will install the most recent version of the `0.4` series.
  However, versions after like `0.5.0` won't be installed, as they may break your build.
  Cargo will automatically upgrade mdBook if you have an older version already installed.
* `--locked` --- This will use the dependencies that were used when mdBook was released.
  Without `--locked`, it will use the latest version of all dependencies, which may include some fixes since the last release, but may also (rarely) cause build problems.

You will likely want to investigate caching options, as building mdBook can be somewhat slow.

[search]: guide/reading.md#search

## Running tests

You may want to run tests using [`mdbook test`] every time you push a change or create a pull request.
This can be used to validate Rust code examples in the book.

This will require having Rust installed.
Some services have Rust pre-installed, but if your service does not, you will need to add a step to install it.

Other than making sure the appropriate version of Rust is installed, there's not much more than just running `mdbook test` from the book directory.

You may also want to consider running other kinds of tests, like [mdbook-linkcheck] which will check for broken links.
Or if you have your own style checks, spell checker, or any other tests it might be good to run them in CI.

[`mdbook test`]: cli/test.md
[mdbook-linkcheck]: https://github.com/Michael-F-Bryan/mdbook-linkcheck#continuous-integration

## Deploying

You may want to automatically deploy your book.
Some may want to do this every time a change is pushed, and others may want to only deploy when a specific release is tagged.

You'll also need to understand the specifics on how to push a change to your web service.
For example, [GitHub Pages] just requires committing the output onto a specific git branch.
Other services may require using something like SSH to connect to a remote server.

The basic outline is that you need to run `mdbook build` to generate the output, and then transfer the files (which are in the `book` directory) to the correct location.

You may then want to consider if you need to invalidate any caches on your web service.

See the [Automated Deployment] wiki page for examples of various different services.

[GitHub Pages]: https://docs.github.com/en/pages

### 404 handling

mdBook automatically generates a 404 page to be used for broken links.
The default output is a file named `404.html` at the root of the book.
Some services like [GitHub Pages] will automatically use this page for broken links.
For other services, you may want to consider configuring the web server to use this page as it will provide the reader navigation to get back to the book.

If your book is not deployed at the root of the domain, then you should set the [`output.html.site-url`] setting so that the 404 page works correctly.
It needs to know where the book is deployed in order to load the static files (like CSS) correctly.
For example, this guide is deployed at <https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/>, and the `site-url` setting is configured like this:

```toml
# book.toml
[output.html]
site-url = "/mdBook/"
```

You can customize the look of the 404 page by creating a file named `src/404.md` in your book.
If you want to use a different filename, you can set [`output.html.input-404`] to a different filename.

[`output.html.site-url`]: format/configuration/renderers.md#html-renderer-options
[`output.html.input-404`]: format/configuration/renderers.md#html-renderer-options

===== guide/src/cli/README.md =====
# Command Line Tool

The `mdbook` command-line tool is used to create and build books.
After you have [installed](../guide/installation.md) `mdbook`, you can run the `mdbook help` command in your terminal to view the available commands.

This following sections provide in-depth information on the different commands available.

* [`mdbook init <directory>`](init.md) --- Creates a new book with minimal boilerplate to start with.
* [`mdbook build`](build.md) --- Renders the book.
* [`mdbook watch`](watch.md) --- Rebuilds the book any time a source file changes.
* [`mdbook serve`](serve.md) --- Runs a web server to view the book, and rebuilds on changes.
* [`mdbook test`](test.md) --- Tests Rust code samples.
* [`mdbook clean`](clean.md) --- Deletes the rendered output.
* [`mdbook completions`](completions.md) --- Support for shell auto-completion.
===== guide/src/cli/init.md =====
# The init command

There is some minimal boilerplate that is the same for every new book. It's for
this purpose that mdBook includes an `init` command.

The `init` command is used like this:

```bash
mdbook init
```

When using the `init` command for the first time, a couple of files will be set
up for you:
```bash
book-test/
├── book
└── src
    ├── chapter_1.md
    └── SUMMARY.md
```

- The `src` directory is where you write your book in markdown. It contains all
  the source files, configuration files, etc.

- The `book` directory is where your book is rendered. All the output is ready
  to be uploaded to a server to be seen by your audience.

- The `SUMMARY.md` is the skeleton of your
  book, and is discussed in more detail [in another
  chapter](../format/summary.md).

#### Tip: Generate chapters from SUMMARY.md

When a `SUMMARY.md` file already exists, the `init` command will first parse it
and generate the missing files according to the paths used in the `SUMMARY.md`.
This allows you to think and create the whole structure of your book and then
let mdBook generate it for you.

#### Specify a directory

The `init` command can take a directory as an argument to use as the book's root
instead of the current working directory.

```bash
mdbook init path/to/book
```

#### `--theme`

When you use the `--theme` flag, the default theme will be copied into a
directory called `theme` in your source directory so that you can modify it.

The theme is selectively overwritten, this means that if you don't want to
overwrite a specific file, just delete it and the default file will be used.

#### `--title`

Specify a title for the book. If not supplied, an interactive prompt will ask for 
a title. 

```bash
mdbook init --title="my amazing book"
```

#### `--ignore`

Create a `.gitignore` file configured to ignore the `book` directory created when [building] a book. 
If not supplied, an interactive prompt will ask whether it should be created.

```bash
mdbook init --ignore=none
```

```bash
mdbook init --ignore=git
```

[building]: build.md

#### `--force`

Skip the prompts to create a `.gitignore` and for the title for the book.
===== guide/src/cli/build.md =====
# The build command

The build command is used to render your book:

```bash
mdbook build
```

It will try to parse your `SUMMARY.md` file to understand the structure of your
book and fetch the corresponding files. Note that this will also create files
mentioned in `SUMMARY.md` which are not yet present.

The rendered output will maintain the same directory structure as the source for
convenience. Large books will therefore remain structured when rendered.

#### Specify a directory

The `build` command can take a directory as an argument to use as the book's
root instead of the current working directory.

```bash
mdbook build path/to/book
```

#### `--open`

When you use the `--open` (`-o`) flag, mdbook will open the rendered book in
your default web browser after building it.

#### `--dest-dir`

The `--dest-dir` (`-d`) option allows you to change the output directory for the
book. Relative paths are interpreted relative to the book's root directory. If
not specified it will default to the value of the `build.build-dir` key in
`book.toml`, or to `./book`.

-------------------

***Note:*** *The build command copies all files (excluding files with `.md` extension) from the source directory
into the build directory.*

===== guide/src/format/configuration/renderers.md =====
# Configuring Renderers

Renderers (also called "backends") are responsible for creating the output of the book.

The following backends are built-in:

* [`html`](#html-renderer-options) --- This renders the book to HTML.
  This is enabled by default if no other `[output]` tables are defined in `book.toml`.
* [`markdown`](#markdown-renderer) --- This outputs the book as markdown after running the preprocessors.
  This is useful for debugging preprocessors.

The community has developed several backends.
See the [Third Party Plugins] wiki page for a list of available backends.

For information on how to create a new backend, see the [Backends for Developers] chapter.

[Third Party Plugins]: https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook/wiki/Third-party-plugins
[Backends for Developers]: ../../for_developers/backends.md

## Output tables

Backends can be added by including a `output` table in `book.toml` with the name of the backend.
For example, if you have a backend called `mdbook-wordcount`, then you can include it with:

```toml
[output.wordcount]
```

With this table, mdBook will execute the `mdbook-wordcount` backend.

This table can include additional key-value pairs that are specific to the backend.
For example, if our example backend needed some extra configuration options:

```toml
[output.wordcount]
ignores = ["Example Chapter"]
```

If you define any `[output]` tables, then the `html` backend is not enabled by default.
If you want to keep the `html` backend running, then just include it in the `book.toml` file.
For example:

```toml
[book]
title = "My Awesome Book"

[output.wordcount]

[output.html]
```

If more than one `output` table is included, this changes the behavior for the layout of the output directory.
If there is only one backend, then it places its output directly in the `book` directory (see [`build.build-dir`] to override this location).
If there is more than one backend, then each backend is placed in a separate directory underneath `book`.
For example, the above would have directories `book/html` and `book/wordcount`.

[`build.build-dir`]: general.md#build-options

### Custom backend commands

By default when you add an `[output.foo]` table to your `book.toml` file,
`mdbook` will try to invoke the `mdbook-foo` executable.
If you want to use a different program name or pass in command-line arguments,
this behaviour can be overridden by adding a `command` field.

```toml
[output.random]
command = "python random.py"
```

### Optional backends

If you enable a backend that isn't installed, the default behavior is to throw an error.
This behavior can be changed by marking the backend as optional:

```toml
[output.wordcount]
optional = true
```

This demotes the error to a warning.


## HTML renderer options

The HTML renderer has a variety of options detailed below.
They should be specified in the `[output.html]` table of the `book.toml` file.

```toml
# Example book.toml file with all output options.
[book]
title = "Example book"
authors = ["John Doe", "Jane Doe"]
description = "The example book covers examples."

[output.html]
theme = "my-theme"
default-theme = "light"
preferred-dark-theme = "navy"
smart-punctuation = true
mathjax-support = false
copy-fonts = true
additional-css = ["custom.css", "custom2.css"]
additional-js = ["custom.js"]
no-section-label = false
git-repository-url = "https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook"
git-repository-icon = "fa-github"
edit-url-template = "https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook/edit/master/guide/{path}"
site-url = "/example-book/"
cname = "myproject.rs"
input-404 = "not-found.md"
```

The following configuration options are available:

- **theme:** mdBook comes with a default theme and all the resource files needed
  for it. But if this option is set, mdBook will selectively overwrite the theme
  files with the ones found in the specified folder.
- **default-theme:** The theme color scheme to select by default in the
  'Change Theme' dropdown. Defaults to `light`.

[`mdbook test`]: ../cli/test.md [rustdoc attributes]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/documentation-tests.html#attributes [editor]: theme/editor.md [`rust.edition`]: configuration/general.md#rust-options ## Including files With the following syntax, you can include files into your book: ```hbs \{{#include file.rs}} ``` The path to the file has to be relative from the current source file. mdBook will interpret included files as Markdown. Since the include command is usually used for inserting code snippets and examples, you will often wrap the command with ```` ``` ```` to display the file contents without interpreting them. ````hbs ``` \{{#include file.rs}} ``` ```` ## Including portions of a file Often you only need a specific part of the file, e.g. relevant lines for an example. We support four different modes of partial includes: ```hbs \{{#include file.rs:2}} \{{#include file.rs::10}} \{{#include file.rs:2:}} \{{#include file.rs:2:10}} ``` The first command only includes the second line from file `file.rs`. The second command includes all lines up to line 10, i.e. the lines from 11 till the end of the file are omitted. The third command includes all lines from line 2, i.e. the first line is omitted. The last command includes the excerpt of `file.rs` consisting of lines 2 to 10. To avoid breaking your book when modifying included files, you can also include a specific section using anchors instead of line numbers. An anchor is a pair of matching lines. The line beginning an anchor must match the regex `ANCHOR:\s*[\w_-]+` and similarly the ending line must match the regex `ANCHOR_END:\s*[\w_-]+`. This allows you to put anchors in any kind of commented line. Consider the following file to include: ```rs /* ANCHOR: all */ // ANCHOR: component struct Paddle { hello: f32, } // ANCHOR_END: component ////////// ANCHOR: system impl System for MySystem { ... } ////////// ANCHOR_END: system /* ANCHOR_END: all */ ``` Then in the book, all you have to do is: ````hbs Here is a component: ```rust,no_run,noplayground \{{#include file.rs:component}} ``` Here is a system: ```rust,no_run,noplayground \{{#include file.rs:system}} ``` This is the full file. ```rust,no_run,noplayground \{{#include file.rs:all}} ``` ```` Lines containing anchor patterns inside the included anchor are ignored. ## Including a file but initially hiding all except specified lines The `rustdoc_include` helper is for including code from external Rust files that contain complete examples, but only initially showing particular lines specified with line numbers or anchors in the same way as with `include`. The lines not in the line number range or between the anchors will still be included, but they will be prefaced with `#`. This way, a reader can expand the snippet to see the complete example, and Rustdoc will use the complete example when you run `mdbook test`. For example, consider a file named `file.rs` that contains this Rust program: ```rust fn main() { let x = add_one(2); assert_eq!(x, 3); } fn add_one(num: i32) -> i32 { num + 1 } ``` We can include a snippet that initially shows only line 2 by using this syntax: ````hbs To call the `add_one` function, we pass it an `i32` and bind the returned value to `x`: ```rust \{{#rustdoc_include file.rs:2}} ``` ```` This would have the same effect as if we had manually inserted the code and hidden all but line 2 using `#`: ````hbs To call the `add_one` function, we pass it an `i32` and bind the returned value to `x`: ```rust # fn main() { let x = add_one(2); # assert_eq!(x, 3); # } # # fn add_one(num: i32) -> i32 { # num + 1 # } ``` ```` That is, it looks like this (click the "expand" icon to see the rest of the file): ```rust # fn main() { let x = add_one(2); # assert_eq!(x, 3); # } # # fn add_one(num: i32) -> i32 { # num + 1 # } ``` ## Inserting runnable Rust files With the following syntax, you can insert runnable Rust files into your book: ```hbs \{{#playground file.rs}} ``` The path to the Rust file has to be relative from the current source file. When play is clicked, the code snippet will be sent to the [Rust Playground] to be compiled and run. The result is sent back and displayed directly underneath the code. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A small, original reimplementation of the mdbook command-line interface.

It is intentionally self contained and uses only the Python standard library.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as _dt
import hashlib
import html as _html
import json
import mimetypes
import os
import posixpath
import re
import shutil
import socketserver
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
from http.server import SimpleHTTPRequestHandler
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

VERSION = "0.5.0-alpha.1"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI help text

TOP_HELP = """Creates a book from markdown files

Usage: {prog} [COMMAND]

Commands:
  init         Creates the boilerplate structure and files for a new book
  build        Builds a book from its markdown files
  test         Tests that a book's Rust code samples compile
  clean        Deletes a built book
  completions  Generate shell completions for your shell to stdout
  watch        Watches a book's files and rebuilds it on changes
  serve        Serves a book at http://localhost:3000, and rebuilds it on changes
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

For more information about a specific command, try `mdbook <command> --help`
The source code for mdBook is available at: https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook
"""

HELP_TEXTS = {
    "init": """Creates the boilerplate structure and files for a new book

Usage: {prog} init [OPTIONS] [dir]

Arguments:
  [dir]  Directory to create the book in
         (Defaults to the current directory when omitted)

Options:
      --theme            Copies the default theme into your source folder
      --force            Skips confirmation prompts

  -h, --help             Print help

""",

Usage: {prog} build [OPTIONS] [dir]

Arguments:

""",

Usage: {prog} clean [OPTIONS] [dir]

Arguments:

Options:

""",
    "completions": """Generate shell completions for your shell to stdout

Usage: {prog} completions <SHELL>

Arguments:
  <SHELL>  the shell to generate completions for [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell,
           zsh]

Options:

""",
    "watch": """Watches a book's files and rebuilds it on changes

Usage: {prog} watch [OPTIONS] [dir]

Arguments:

Options:

""",

Usage: {prog} serve [OPTIONS] [dir]

SUBCOMMANDS = ["init", "build", "test", "clean", "completions", "watch", "serve", "help"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diagnostics and small utilities

class MdBookError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message: str, causes: Optional[List[str]] = None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        self.causes = causes or []


def _ts() -> str:
    return _dt.datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")


def log(level: str, target: str, message: str) -> None:
    print(f"{_ts()} [{level}] ({target}): {message}", file=sys.stderr)


def log_error(message: str, causes: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> None:
    log("ERROR", "mdbook_core::utils", f"Error: {message}")
    for cause in causes or []:
        log("ERROR", "mdbook_core::utils", f"\tCaused By: {cause}")


def die_runtime(message: str, causes: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> None:
    log_error(message, causes)
    raise SystemExit(101)


def clap_error(message: str, usage: Optional[str] = None, tip: Optional[str] = None, values: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    print(f"error: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
    if values:
        print(values, file=sys.stderr)
    if tip:
        print(f"\n  tip: {tip}", file=sys.stderr)
    if usage:
        print(f"\nUsage: {usage}", file=sys.stderr)
    print("\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(2)


def print_help(cmd: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    prog = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) or "executable"
    if cmd is None:
        sys.stdout.write(TOP_HELP.format(prog=prog))
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXTS[cmd].format(prog=prog))


def print_help_err() -> None:
    prog = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) or "executable"
    sys.stderr.write(TOP_HELP.format(prog=prog))


def posix_rel(p: Path, base: Path) -> str:
    return os.path.relpath(str(p), str(base)).replace(os.sep, "/")


def norm_join(root: Path, rel: str) -> Path:
    # Pathlib intentionally normalizes the doubled slash in strings such as
    # "https://example.com" to the on-disk path mdBook also creates:
    # "https:/example.com".
    return root.joinpath(Path(rel))


def html_escape_text(s: str) -> str:
    # pulldown-cmark allows inline HTML. Escape ampersands so ordinary text is
    # valid HTML, but leave tags alone.
    return s.replace("&", "&")


def attr_escape(s: str) -> str:
    return _html.escape(s, quote=True)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Minimal TOML reader (sufficient for book.toml files used by mdBook docs)


def strip_toml_comment(line: str) -> str:
    in_s = False
    in_d = False
    esc = False
    out = []
    for ch in line:
        if in_d and esc:
            out.append(ch); esc = False; continue
        if in_d and ch == "\\":
            out.append(ch); esc = True; continue
        if ch == '"' and not in_s:
            in_d = not in_d
        elif ch == "'" and not in_d:
            in_s = not in_s
        elif ch == "#" and not in_s and not in_d:
            break
        out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out).strip()


def parse_toml_value(v: str) -> Any:
    v = v.strip()
    if not v:
        return ""
    if v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"') and len(v) >= 2:
        try:
            return bytes(v[1:-1], "utf-8").decode("unicode_escape")
        except Exception:
            return v[1:-1]
    if v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'") and len(v) >= 2:
        return v[1:-1]
    if v.startswith("["):
        if not v.endswith("]"):
            raise ValueError("unclosed array, expected `]`")
        inner = v[1:-1].strip()
        if not inner:
            return []
        vals: List[str] = []
        cur = ""
        in_s = in_d = False
        esc = False
        parts: List[str] = []
        for ch in inner:
            if in_d and esc:
                cur += ch; esc = False; continue
            if in_d and ch == "\\":
                cur += ch; esc = True; continue
            if ch == '"' and not in_s:
                in_d = not in_d; cur += ch; continue
            if ch == "'" and not in_d:
                in_s = not in_s; cur += ch; continue
            if ch == "," and not in_s and not in_d:
                parts.append(cur.strip()); cur = ""; continue
            cur += ch
        if cur.strip():
            parts.append(cur.strip())
        return [parse_toml_value(p) for p in parts]
    if v.lower() == "true":
        return True
    if v.lower() == "false":
        return False
    if re.fullmatch(r"[+-]?\d+", v):
        try:
            return int(v)
        except Exception:
            pass
    return v


def parse_key(k: str) -> str:
    k = k.strip()
    if (k.startswith('"') and k.endswith('"')) or (k.startswith("'") and k.endswith("'")):
        return k[1:-1]
    return k


def parse_toml(path: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    root: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    if not path.exists():
        return root
    table: List[str] = []
    try:
        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        lines = path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
    for idx, raw in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        line = strip_toml_comment(raw)
        if not line:
            continue
        if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
            inner = line.strip("[]").strip()
            table = [parse_key(p) for p in inner.split(".") if p.strip()]
            d = root
            for p in table:
                d = d.setdefault(p, {})
            continue
        if "=" in line:
            k, v = line.split("=", 1)
            key = parse_key(k)
            d = root
            for p in table:
                d = d.setdefault(p, {})
            try:
                d[key] = parse_toml_value(v)
            except ValueError as e:
                # A close facsimile of toml_edit's diagnostic for the common
                # invalid cases.
                caret_col = raw.find("=") + 2 if "=" in raw else 1
                cause = f"TOML parse error at line {idx}, column {caret_col}\n  |\n{idx} | {raw}\n  | {' ' * max(caret_col-1,0)}^\n{e}"
                raise MdBookError("Invalid configuration file", [cause])
    return root


def get_in(d: Dict[str, Any], path: List[str], default: Any = None) -> Any:
    cur: Any = d
    for p in path:
        if not isinstance(cur, dict) or p not in cur:
            return default
        cur = cur[p]
    return cur


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Summary parsing and book loading

class Chapter:
    def __init__(self, title: str = "", path: str = "", level: int = 1, affix: bool = False,
                 draft: bool = False, kind: str = "chapter", number: str = ""):
        self.title = title
        self.path = path
        self.level = level
        self.affix = affix
        self.draft = draft
        self.kind = kind  # chapter, part, spacer
        self.number = number
        self.children: List[Chapter] = []
        self.parent: Optional[Chapter] = None
        self.href = chapter_href(path) if path else ""
        self.fs_href = self.href
        self.content = ""
        self.main_html = ""
        self.headings: List[Tuple[int, str, str]] = []
        self.page_title_override: Optional[str] = None

    def is_page(self) -> bool:
        return self.kind == "chapter" and bool(self.path) and not self.draft


def chapter_href(path: str) -> str:
    if not path:
        return ""
    p = path.split("#", 1)[0]
    frag = "#" + path.split("#", 1)[1] if "#" in path else ""
    # Preserve doubled slashes in href strings such as https://example.com; only
    # change the final component extension.
    parts = p.rsplit("/", 1)
    dirname = parts[0] + "/" if len(parts) == 2 else ""
    base = parts[-1]
    lower = base.lower()
    if lower == "readme.md":
        outbase = "index.html"
    elif lower.endswith(".md"):
        outbase = base[:-3] + ".html"
    elif "." in base:
        outbase = base.rsplit(".", 1)[0] + ".html"
    else:
        outbase = base + ".html"
    return dirname + outbase + frag


def source_title(title: str) -> str:
    return f"# {title}\n"


def parse_summary(summary: Path) -> List[Chapter]:
    try:
        lines = summary.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        lines = summary.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
    chapters: List[Chapter] = []
    counters: List[int] = []
    used: set[str] = set()
    root_stack: Dict[int, Chapter] = {}
    for raw in lines:
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        if stripped.lower() == "# summary":
            continue
        if re.fullmatch(r"-{3,}", stripped):
            chapters.append(Chapter(kind="spacer"))
            continue
        if stripped.startswith("#") and not re.search(r"\[[^\]]+\]\([^)]*\)", stripped):
            title = stripped.lstrip("#").strip()
            if title and title.lower() != "summary":
                chapters.append(Chapter(title=title, kind="part", affix=True, level=0))
            continue
        m = re.search(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]*)\)", raw)
        if not m:
            # mdBook ignores much prose in SUMMARY.md; malformed list links are
            # uncommon, so leave them alone here.
            continue
        title = m.group(1).strip()
        target = m.group(2).strip()
        bullet = re.match(r"^(\s*)[-*+]\s+", raw)
        if target:
            if target in used:
                raise MdBookError(f"Summary parsing failed for file=\"{summary}\"", [f"Duplicate file in SUMMARY.md: \"{target}\""])
            used.add(target)
        if bullet:
            spaces = len(bullet.group(1).replace("\t", "    "))
            level = spaces // 2 + 1
            while len(counters) < level:
                counters.append(0)
            counters = counters[:level]
            counters[level-1] += 1
            number = ".".join(str(x) for x in counters)
            ch = Chapter(title, target, level, affix=False, draft=(target == ""), number=number)
        else:
            ch = Chapter(title, target, 0, affix=True, draft=(target == ""), number="")
        chapters.append(ch)
    # Build hierarchy for TOC rendering.
    stack: List[Chapter] = []
    for ch in chapters:
        if ch.kind != "chapter" or ch.affix or ch.level <= 0:
            stack = [] if ch.kind in ("part", "spacer") else stack
            continue
        while stack and stack[-1].level >= ch.level:
            stack.pop()
        if stack:
            ch.parent = stack[-1]
            stack[-1].children.append(ch)
        stack.append(ch)
    return chapters


class Book:
    def __init__(self, root: Path, cfg: Dict[str, Any], chapters: List[Chapter]):
        self.root = root
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.chapters = chapters
        self.src_dir = root / str(get_in(cfg, ["book", "src"], "src"))
        self.title = str(get_in(cfg, ["book", "title"], "") or "")
        self.description = str(get_in(cfg, ["book", "description"], "") or "")
        self.language = str(get_in(cfg, ["book", "language"], "en") or "en")
        self.edition = str(get_in(cfg, ["rust", "edition"], "2015") or "2015")

    def build_dir_name(self) -> str:
        return str(get_in(self.cfg, ["build", "build-dir"], "book") or "book")

    def create_missing(self) -> bool:
        return bool(get_in(self.cfg, ["build", "create-missing"], True))

    def html_cfg(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        val = get_in(self.cfg, ["output", "html"], {})
        return val if isinstance(val, dict) else {}


def load_book(root_arg: str = ".", create: bool = True, check_missing: bool = True) -> Book:
    root = Path(root_arg)
    if not root.is_absolute():
        root = Path.cwd() / root
    try:
        cfg = parse_toml(root / "book.toml")
    except MdBookError as e:
        die_runtime(e.message, e.causes)
    src_dir = root / str(get_in(cfg, ["book", "src"], "src") or "src")
    summary = src_dir / "SUMMARY.md"
    if not summary.exists():
        die_runtime(f"Couldn't open SUMMARY.md in \"{src_dir}\" directory", ["No such file or directory (os error 2)"])
    try:
        chapters = parse_summary(summary)
    except MdBookError as e:
        # parse_summary embeds the leading message for duplicate errors.
        if e.message.startswith("Summary parsing failed"):
            log_error(e.message, e.causes)
            raise SystemExit(101)
        die_runtime(e.message, e.causes)
    book = Book(root, cfg, chapters)
    if check_missing:
        for ch in chapters:
            if ch.is_page():
                sp = norm_join(book.src_dir, ch.path)
                if not sp.exists():
                    if book.create_missing() and create:
                        sp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                        sp.write_text(source_title(ch.title), encoding="utf-8")
                    else:
                        die_runtime(f"Chapter file not found, {ch.path}", ["No such file or directory (os error 2)"])
    return book


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# init command

THEME_FILES = {
    "book.js": "// mdBook theme JavaScript placeholder\n",
    "css/chrome.css": "/* mdBook chrome stylesheet */\n",
    "css/general.css": "/* mdBook general stylesheet */\n",
    "css/print.css": "/* mdBook print stylesheet */\n",
    "css/variables.css": ":root { --bg: #fff; --fg: #000; }\n",
    "favicon.svg": "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\"><text y=\"14\">M</text></svg>\n",
    "favicon.png": b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n",
    "fonts/OPEN-SANS-LICENSE.txt": "Open Sans license placeholder\n",
    "fonts/SOURCE-CODE-PRO-LICENSE.txt": "Source Code Pro license placeholder\n",
    "fonts/fonts.css": "/* font-face declarations placeholder */\n",
    "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-300.woff2": b"",
    "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-300italic.woff2": b"",
    "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-600.woff2": b"",
    "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-600italic.woff2": b"",
    "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-700.woff2": b"",
    "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-700italic.woff2": b"",
    "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-800.woff2": b"",
    "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-800italic.woff2": b"",
    "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-italic.woff2": b"",
    "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-regular.woff2": b"",
    "fonts/source-code-pro-v11-all-charsets-500.woff2": b"",
    "highlight.css": "/* highlight.js default theme */\n",
    "highlight.js": "// highlight.js placeholder\n",
    "index.hbs": "<!DOCTYPE HTML>\n<html><head><title>{{ title }}</title></head><body>{{ content }}</body></html>\n",
}


def copy_theme(dest: Path) -> None:
    for rel, content in THEME_FILES.items():
        p = dest / rel
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if isinstance(content, bytes):
            p.write_bytes(content)
        else:
            p.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")


def init_book(args: List[str]) -> None:
    prog = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) or "executable"
    if any(a in ("-h", "--help") for a in args):
        print_help("init"); return
    if any(a in ("-V", "--version") for a in args):
        print(f"mdbook-init v{VERSION}"); return
    theme = False
    force = False
    title: Optional[str] = None
    ignore: Optional[str] = None
    positionals: List[str] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if a == "--theme":
            theme = True; i += 1
        elif a.startswith("--theme="):
            val = a.split("=", 1)[1]
            clap_error(f"unexpected value '{val}' for '--theme' found; no more were expected", f"{prog} init --theme [dir]")
        elif a == "--force":
            force = True; i += 1
        elif a == "--title":
            if i + 1 >= len(args):
                clap_error("a value is required for '--title <title>' but none was supplied")
            title = args[i+1]; i += 2
        elif a.startswith("--title="):
            title = a.split("=", 1)[1]; i += 1
        elif a == "--ignore":
            if i + 1 >= len(args):
                clap_error("a value is required for '--ignore <ignore>' but none was supplied")
            ignore = args[i+1]; i += 2
        elif a.startswith("--ignore="):
            ignore = a.split("=", 1)[1]; i += 1
        elif a.startswith("-"):
            clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{a}' found", f"{prog} init [OPTIONS] [dir]", tip=f"to pass '{a}' as a value, use '-- {a}'")
        else:
            positionals.append(a); i += 1
    if ignore is not None and ignore not in ("none", "git"):
        clap_error(f"invalid value '{ignore}' for '--ignore <ignore>'", values="  [possible values: none, git]")
    if len(positionals) > 1:
        clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{positionals[1]}' found", f"{prog} init [OPTIONS] [dir]")
    root = Path(positionals[0] if positionals else ".")
    if not root.is_absolute():
        root = Path.cwd() / root

    create_gitignore = False
    if ignore is None and not force:
        print("\nDo you want a .gitignore to be created? (y/n)")
        ans = sys.stdin.readline().strip().lower()
        create_gitignore = ans in ("y", "yes")
    elif ignore == "git":
        create_gitignore = True

    if title is None and not force:
        print("What title would you like to give the book? ")
        title = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip("\n\r")

    log("INFO", "mdbook_driver::init", "Creating a new book with stub content")
    try:
        root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (root / "src").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (root / "book").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    except OSError as e:
        log_error("Unable to create directory structure", [f"{e.strerror} (os error {getattr(e, 'errno', 0)})"])
        raise SystemExit(101)

    bt = '[book]\nauthors = []\nlanguage = "en"\nsrc = "src"\n'
    if title is not None and title != "":
        bt += f'title = "{title}"\n'
    elif title == "":
        # Explicit --title "" is preserved; an empty interactive answer is not.
        if any(a == "--title" or a.startswith("--title=") for a in args):
            bt += 'title = ""\n'
    (root / "book.toml").write_text(bt, encoding="utf-8")

    summary = root / "src" / "SUMMARY.md"
    if not summary.exists():
        summary.write_text("# Summary\n\n- [Chapter 1](./chapter_1.md)\n", encoding="utf-8")
        chap = root / "src" / "chapter_1.md"
        if not chap.exists():
            chap.write_text("# Chapter 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        try:
            chapters = parse_summary(summary)
        except MdBookError:
            chapters = []
        for ch in chapters:
            if ch.path:
                p = norm_join(root / "src", ch.path)
                if not p.exists():
                    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    p.write_text(source_title(ch.title), encoding="utf-8")

    if create_gitignore:
        (root / ".gitignore").write_text("book\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if theme:
        theme_dir = root / "theme"
        print(f"\nCopying the default theme to {theme_dir}")
        copy_theme(theme_dir)
    print("\nAll done, no errors...")

INCLUDE_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!\\)\{\{#(include|rustdoc_include|playground)\s+([^}]+?)\}\}")
TITLE_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^\s*\{\{#title\s+([^}]+?)\}\}\s*$")


def split_include_spec(spec: str) -> Tuple[str, Optional[str], List[str]]:
    parts = spec.strip().split()
    first = parts[0] if parts else ""
    attrs = parts[1:]
    if ":" in first:
        # Keep Windows paths out of scope; mdBook specs use path:range.
        path, rest = first.split(":", 1)
        return path, rest, attrs
    return first, None, attrs


def select_lines(text: str, selector: Optional[str], rustdoc: bool = False) -> str:
    if not selector:
        return text
    lines = text.splitlines(True)
    # line ranges: N, :N, N:, N:M
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d*:?\d*", selector or ""):
        if ":" in selector:
            a, b = selector.split(":", 1)
            start = int(a) if a else 1
            end = int(b) if b else len(lines)
        else:
            start = end = int(selector)
        selected = lines[max(start-1, 0):min(end, len(lines))]
        if rustdoc:
            out = []
            for idx, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
                if start <= idx <= end:
                    out.append(line)
                else:
                    out.append("# " + line if line.strip() else "#\n")
            return "".join(out)
        return "".join(selected)
    # anchor ranges
    name = selector
    start_re = re.compile(r"ANCHOR:\s*" + re.escape(name) + r"\b")
    end_re = re.compile(r"ANCHOR_END:\s*" + re.escape(name) + r"\b")
    inside = False
    out: List[str] = []
    for line in lines:
        if not inside and start_re.search(line):
            inside = True; continue
        if inside and end_re.search(line):
            inside = False; break
        if inside and not re.search(r"ANCHOR(_END)?:", line):
            out.append(line)
    return "".join(out) if out else text


def preprocess_content(book: Book, ch: Chapter, text: str) -> str:
    base_dir = norm_join(book.src_dir, ch.path).parent if ch.path else book.src_dir

    def repl(m: re.Match) -> str:
        kind, spec = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()
        path_part, selector, attrs = split_include_spec(spec)
        fp = norm_join(base_dir, path_part)
        try:
            data = fp.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except Exception:
            log("ERROR", "mdbook_driver::builtin_preprocessors::links", f"Error updating \"{{{{#{kind} {spec}}}}}\", Could not read file for link {{{{#{kind} {spec}}}}} ({fp})")
            log("WARN", "mdbook_driver::builtin_preprocessors::links", "Caused By: No such file or directory (os error 2)")
            return m.group(0)
        if kind == "playground":
            attr = ("," + ",".join(attrs)) if attrs else ""
            return f"```rust{attr}\n{data.rstrip()}\n```"
        return select_lines(data, selector, rustdoc=(kind == "rustdoc_include"))

    text = INCLUDE_RE.sub(repl, text)
    text = text.replace(r"\{{#", "{{#")
    return text


def slugify(text: str, used: Dict[str, int]) -> str:
    # Drop HTML tags for the slug, lower-case, keep unicode alnum, '_' and '-'.
    no_tags = re.sub(r"<[^>]*>", "", text)
    no_tags = no_tags.lower()
    out = []
    for ch in no_tags:
        if ch.isalnum() or ch in "_-":
            out.append(ch)
        elif ch.isspace():
            out.append("-")
        else:
            # punctuation disappears
            pass
    base = "".join(out).strip("-") or "section"
    n = used.get(base, 0)
    used[base] = n + 1
    return base if n == 0 else f"{base}-{n}"


def convert_link_url(url: str) -> str:
    if re.match(r"^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*://", url) or url.startswith("mailto:"):
        return url
    if url.startswith("#"):
        return url
    frag = ""
    if "#" in url:
        url, frag = url.split("#", 1)
        frag = "#" + frag
    if url.lower().endswith(".md"):
        return chapter_href(url) + frag
    return url + frag


def parse_inline(s: str) -> str:
    placeholders: List[str] = []

    def hold(val: str) -> str:
        placeholders.append(val)
        return f"\x00{len(placeholders)-1}\x00"

    def code_repl(m: re.Match) -> str:
        return hold(f"<code>{_html.escape(m.group(1))}</code>")

    s = re.sub(r"`([^`]+)`", code_repl, s)

    def img_repl(m: re.Match) -> str:
        alt = attr_escape(m.group(1))
        src = attr_escape(convert_link_url(m.group(2)))
        return hold(f'<img src="{src}" alt="{alt}" />')

    s = re.sub(r"!\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]+)\)", img_repl, s)

    def link_repl(m: re.Match) -> str:
        txt = parse_inline(m.group(1))
        href = attr_escape(convert_link_url(m.group(2)))
        return hold(f'<a href="{href}">{txt}</a>')

    s = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+)\)", link_repl, s)
    s = html_escape_text(s)
    s = re.sub(r"\*\*([^*]+)\*\*", r"<strong>\1</strong>", s)
    s = re.sub(r"(?<!\*)\*([^*]+)\*(?!\*)", r"<em>\1</em>", s)
    s = re.sub(r"__([^_]+)__", r"<strong>\1</strong>", s)
    s = re.sub(r"(?<!_)_([^_]+)_(?!_)", r"<em>\1</em>", s)
    for i, val in enumerate(placeholders):
        s = s.replace(f"\x00{i}\x00", val)
    return s


def render_markdown_to_html(md: str, smart: bool = False) -> Tuple[str, List[Tuple[int, str, str]], str]:
    if smart:
        md = md.replace("---", "—").replace("--", "–")
    lines = md.splitlines()
    out: List[str] = []
    headings: List[Tuple[int, str, str]] = []
    plain_parts: List[str] = []
    used_slugs: Dict[str, int] = {}
    i = 0
    para: List[str] = []

    def flush_para() -> None:
        nonlocal para
        if para:
            text = " ".join(x.strip() for x in para).strip()
            if text:
                out.append(f"<p>{parse_inline(text)}</p>")
                plain_parts.append(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", parse_inline(text)))
            para = []

    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped:
            flush_para(); i += 1; continue
        fence = re.match(r"^\s*(```+|~~~+)\s*([^`]*)$", line)
        if fence:
            flush_para()
            marker = fence.group(1)[:3]
            info = fence.group(2).strip()
            code_lines: List[str] = []
            i += 1
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].lstrip().startswith(marker):
                code_lines.append(lines[i]); i += 1
            if i < len(lines):
                i += 1
            code = _html.escape("\n".join(code_lines))
            lang = info.split(",", 1)[0].strip()
            cls = f' class="language-{attr_escape(lang)}"' if lang else ""
            if lang in ("rust", "rs") or info.startswith("rust"):
                out.append(f'<pre><pre class="playground"><code class="language-rust">{code}</code></pre></pre>')
            else:
                out.append(f"<pre><code{cls}>{code}</code></pre>")
            plain_parts.append("\n".join(code_lines))
            continue
        hm = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$", line)
        if hm:
            flush_para()
            level = len(hm.group(1))
            title = hm.group(2).strip()
            sid = slugify(title, used_slugs)
            headings.append((level, title, sid))
            out.append(f'<h{level} id="{sid}"><a class="header" href="#{sid}">{parse_inline(title)}</a></h{level}>')
            plain_parts.append(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", title))
            i += 1; continue
        if re.match(r"^\s*([-*+])\s+", line):
            flush_para()
            out.append("<ul>")
            while i < len(lines) and re.match(r"^\s*([-*+])\s+", lines[i]):
                item = re.sub(r"^\s*[-*+]\s+", "", lines[i]).strip()
                out.append(f"<li>{parse_inline(item)}</li>")
                plain_parts.append(item)
                i += 1
            out.append("</ul>")
            continue
        if re.match(r"^\s*\d+\.\s+", line):
            flush_para()
            out.append("<ol>")
            while i < len(lines) and re.match(r"^\s*\d+\.\s+", lines[i]):
                item = re.sub(r"^\s*\d+\.\s+", "", lines[i]).strip()
                out.append(f"<li>{parse_inline(item)}</li>")
                plain_parts.append(item)
                i += 1
            out.append("</ol>")
            continue
        if stripped.startswith(">"):
            flush_para()
            bq: List[str] = []
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].lstrip().startswith(">"):
                bq.append(lines[i].lstrip()[1:].strip())
                i += 1
            inner, _, _ = render_markdown_to_html("\n".join(bq), smart=False)
            out.append(f"<blockquote>\n{inner}\n</blockquote>")
            continue
        if re.fullmatch(r"[-*_]{3,}", stripped):
            flush_para(); out.append("<hr />"); i += 1; continue
        # Simple pipe table.
        if "|" in line and i + 1 < len(lines) and re.match(r"^\s*\|?\s*:?-{3,}:?", lines[i+1]):
            flush_para()
            headers = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
            i += 2
            rows: List[List[str]] = []
            while i < len(lines) and "|" in lines[i] and lines[i].strip():
                rows.append([c.strip() for c in lines[i].strip().strip("|").split("|")]); i += 1
            out.append("<table><thead><tr>" + "".join(f"<th>{parse_inline(c)}</th>" for c in headers) + "</tr></thead><tbody>")
            for r in rows:
                out.append("<tr>" + "".join(f"<td>{parse_inline(c)}</td>" for c in r) + "</tr>")
            out.append("</tbody></table>")
            continue
        if stripped.startswith("<") and stripped.endswith(">"):
            flush_para(); out.append(line); i += 1; continue
        para.append(line)
        i += 1
    flush_para()
    return "\n".join(out), headings, " ".join(plain_parts)

def write_file(path: Path, content: Any) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if isinstance(content, bytes):
        path.write_bytes(content)
    else:
        path.write_text(str(content), encoding="utf-8")


def copy_static_assets(out: Path, book: Book, search_enabled: bool, editable: bool = False, copy_fonts: bool = True) -> None:
    write_file(out / ".nojekyll", NOJEKYLL)
    for rel, content in THEME_FILES.items():
        if rel == "index.hbs":
            continue
        if not copy_fonts and (rel.startswith("fonts/") or rel.startswith("FontAwesome/")):
            continue
        write_file(out / rel, content)
    for rel, content in STATIC_FILES.items():
        if not search_enabled and rel in ("elasticlunr.min.js", "mark.min.js", "searcher.js"):
            continue
        write_file(out / rel, content)
    if editable:
        for rel in ["ace.js", "editor.js", "mode-rust.js", "theme-dawn.js", "theme-tomorrow_night.js"]:
            write_file(out / rel, f"// {rel} placeholder\n")


def copy_source_static(book: Book, out: Path) -> None:
    if not book.src_dir.exists():
        return
    for p in book.src_dir.rglob("*"):
        if not p.is_file():
            continue
        rel = p.relative_to(book.src_dir).as_posix()
        if rel == "SUMMARY.md" or p.suffix.lower() == ".md":
            continue
        dest = out / rel
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            shutil.copy2(p, dest)
        except shutil.SameFileError:
            pass


def rel_depth(href: str) -> int:
    h = href.split("#", 1)[0]
    if "/" not in h:
        return 0
    return max(len([x for x in h.split("/")[:-1] if x]), 0)


def root_prefix(href: str) -> str:
    return "../" * rel_depth(href)


def page_title(book: Book, ch: Chapter) -> str:
    if ch.page_title_override:
        return ch.page_title_override
    return f"{ch.title} - {book.title}" if book.title else ch.title


def edit_url(book: Book, ch: Optional[Chapter]) -> str:
    tmpl = str(get_in(book.cfg, ["output", "html", "edit-url-template"], "") or "")
    if not tmpl or ch is None or not ch.path:
        return ""
    src = str(get_in(book.cfg, ["book", "src"], "src") or "src")
    return tmpl.replace("{path}", f"{src}/{ch.path}")

def top_level_items(chapters: List[Chapter]) -> List[Chapter]:
    return [c for c in chapters if c.kind != "chapter" or c.affix or c.level <= 1]


def toc_item(ch: Chapter, target_parent: bool, no_labels: bool) -> str:
    if ch.kind == "part":
        return f'<li class="part-title">{html_escape_text(ch.title)}</li>'
    if ch.kind == "spacer":
        return '<li class="spacer"></li>'
    label = "" if (no_labels or ch.affix or not ch.number) else f'<strong aria-hidden="true">{ch.number}.</strong> '
    aff = "affix " if ch.affix else ""
    if ch.draft or not ch.path:
        body = f'<div>{label}{html_escape_text(ch.title)}</div>'
    else:
        tgt = ' target="_parent"' if target_parent else ""
        body = f'<a href="{attr_escape(ch.href)}"{tgt}>{label}{html_escape_text(ch.title)}</a>'
    s = f'<li class="chapter-item expanded {aff}">{body}</li>'
    if ch.children:
        s += '<li><ol class="section">' + "".join(toc_item(c, target_parent, no_labels) for c in ch.children) + '</ol></li>'
    return s


def render_toc(book: Book, target_parent: bool = True) -> str:
    no_labels = bool(get_in(book.cfg, ["output", "html", "no-section-label"], False))
    items = top_level_items(book.chapters)
    return '<ol class="chapter">' + "".join(toc_item(c, target_parent, no_labels) for c in items) + '</ol>'


def render_toc_html(book: Book, search_enabled: bool, additional_css: List[str], asset_map: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None) -> str:

def render_toc_js(book: Book) -> str:
    inner = render_toc(book, target_parent=False).replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'")
    return f'''// Populate the sidebar
//
// This is a script, and not included directly in the page, to control the total size of the book.
class MDBookSidebarScrollbox extends HTMLElement {{
    constructor() {{ super(); }}
    connectedCallback() {{
        this.innerHTML = '{inner}';
        let current_page = document.location.href.toString().split("#")[0].split("?")[0];
        if (current_page.endsWith("/")) {{ current_page += "index.html"; }}
        var links = Array.prototype.slice.call(this.querySelectorAll("a"));
        for (var i = 0; i < links.length; ++i) {{
            var link = links[i];
            var href = link.getAttribute("href");
            if (href && !href.startsWith("#") && !/^(?:[a-z+]+:)?\/\//.test(href)) {{ link.href = path_to_root + href; }}
            if (link.href === current_page || (i === 0 && path_to_root === "" && current_page.endsWith("/index.html"))) {{ link.classList.add("active"); }}
        }}
    }}
}}
window.customElements.define("mdbook-sidebar-scrollbox", MDBookSidebarScrollbox);
'''


def render_search_index(book: Book, pages: List[Chapter]) -> str:
    docs = []
    urls = []
    for idx, ch in enumerate(pages):
        if ch.headings:
            level, htitle, sid = ch.headings[0]
            url = f"{ch.href}#{sid}"
            title = htitle
        else:
            url = ch.href
            title = ch.title
        urls.append(url)
        crumb = ch.title + (f" » {title}" if title != ch.title else "")
        body = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", ch.main_html)).strip()
        docs.append({"id": str(idx), "title": title, "body": body, "breadcrumbs": crumb})
    data = {
        "doc_urls": urls,
        "index": {"documentStore": {"docs": {str(i): d for i, d in enumerate(docs)}, "length": len(docs), "save": True}, "fields": ["title", "body", "breadcrumbs"]},
        "results_options": {"limit_results": int(get_in(book.cfg, ["output", "html", "search", "limit-results"], 30) or 30), "teaser_word_count": 30},
        "search_options": {"bool": "AND" if get_in(book.cfg, ["output", "html", "search", "use-boolean-and"], False) else "OR", "expand": bool(get_in(book.cfg, ["output", "html", "search", "expand"], True)), "fields": {"body": {"boost": 1}, "breadcrumbs": {"boost": 1}, "title": {"boost": 2}}},
    }
    js = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False).replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'")
    return f"window.search = Object.assign(window.search, JSON.parse('{js}'));\n"


def render_redirect(target: str) -> str:
    esc = attr_escape(target)
    return f'''<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <title>Redirecting...</title>
    <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; URL={esc}">
    <link rel="canonical" href="{esc}">
  </head>
  <body>
      <p>Redirecting to... <a href="{esc}">{html_escape_text(target)}</a>.</p>

<script>
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {{
        const fragment = window.location.hash;
        if (fragment) {{
            let url = new URL("{esc}", window.location.href);
            url.hash = window.location.hash;
            window.location.replace(url.href);
        }}
    }});
</script>
  </body>
</html>
'''


def apply_hashes(out: Path) -> Dict[str, str]:
    candidates: List[Path] = []
    for p in out.rglob("*"):
        if not p.is_file():
            continue
        rel = p.relative_to(out).as_posix()
        if p.suffix.lower() in (".html", "") or rel in (".nojekyll", "CNAME"):
            continue
        candidates.append(p)
    mapping: Dict[str, str] = {}
    for p in candidates:
        rel = p.relative_to(out).as_posix()
        data = p.read_bytes()
        h = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()[:8]
        new_name = f"{p.stem}-{h}{p.suffix}"
        new_rel = (p.parent.relative_to(out) / new_name).as_posix()
        mapping[rel] = new_rel
    # Rename deepest first to avoid path collisions.
    for old_rel, new_rel in sorted(mapping.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[0].count("/"), reverse=True):
        src = out / old_rel
        dst = out / new_rel
        dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if src.exists():
            src.rename(dst)
    # Rewrite textual references.
    text_exts = {".html", ".js", ".css"}
    # Replace long paths before basenames.
    replacements: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
    for old, new in mapping.items():
        replacements.append((old, new))
        replacements.append((posixpath.basename(old), posixpath.basename(new)))
    replacements.sort(key=lambda x: len(x[0]), reverse=True)
    for p in out.rglob("*"):
        if not p.is_file() or p.suffix.lower() not in text_exts:
            continue
        try:
            txt = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except Exception:
            continue
        nt = txt
        for old, new in replacements:
            nt = nt.replace(old, new)
        if nt != txt:
            p.write_text(nt, encoding="utf-8")
    return mapping


def output_renderers(cfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[str]:
    out = cfg.get("output")
    if not isinstance(out, dict) or not out:
        return ["html"]
    # If only nested html subtables are present, html is enabled. Preserve a
    # stable mdBook-like order for built-ins.
    names = list(out.keys())
    ordered: List[str] = []
    for n in ["markdown", "html"]:
        if n in names:
            ordered.append(n)
    for n in names:
        if n not in ordered:
            ordered.append(n)
    return ordered


def renderer_out_dir(book: Book, name: str, dest_dir: Optional[str], renderers: List[str]) -> Path:
    build_dir = dest_dir if dest_dir is not None else book.build_dir_name()
    base = Path(build_dir)
    if not base.is_absolute():
        base = book.root / base
    if len(renderers) > 1:
        base = base / name
    return base


def warn_index_collisions(book: Book) -> None:
    dirs: Dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for ch in book.chapters:
        if not ch.path:
            continue
        pp = PurePosixPath(ch.path)
        dirs.setdefault(str(pp.parent) if str(pp.parent) != "." else "", set()).add(pp.name.lower())
    for d, names in dirs.items():
        if "readme.md" in names and "index.md" in names:
            src = book.src_dir / d
            log("WARN", "mdbook_driver::builtin_preprocessors::index", f"It seems that there are both \"README.md\" and index.md under \"{src}\".")
            log("WARN", "mdbook_driver::builtin_preprocessors::index", 'mdbook converts "README.md" into index.html by default. It may cause')
            log("WARN", "mdbook_driver::builtin_preprocessors::index", "unexpected behavior if putting both files under the same directory.")
            log("WARN", "mdbook_driver::builtin_preprocessors::index", "To solve the warning, try to rearrange the book structure or disable")
            log("WARN", "mdbook_driver::builtin_preprocessors::index", '"index" preprocessor to stop the conversion.')


def render_html_backend(book: Book, out: Path) -> None:
    html_cfg = book.html_cfg()
    search_cfg = html_cfg.get("search", {}) if isinstance(html_cfg.get("search", {}), dict) else {}
    search_enabled = bool(search_cfg.get("enable", True))
    playground_cfg = html_cfg.get("playground", {}) if isinstance(html_cfg.get("playground", {}), dict) else {}
    editable = bool(playground_cfg.get("editable", False))
    copy_fonts = bool(html_cfg.get("copy-fonts", True))
    smart = bool(html_cfg.get("smart-punctuation", False))
    mathjax = bool(html_cfg.get("mathjax-support", False))
    additional_css = list(html_cfg.get("additional-css", []) or [])
    additional_js = list(html_cfg.get("additional-js", []) or [])

    if out.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    copy_source_static(book, out)
    copy_static_assets(out, book, search_enabled, editable, copy_fonts)

    # Additional assets are relative to the book root.
    for rel in additional_css + additional_js:
        src = book.root / rel
        if not src.exists():
            die_runtime("Rendering failed", ["Unable to copy across static files", "No such file or directory (os error 2)"])
        dest = out / rel
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(src, dest)

    cname = html_cfg.get("cname")
    if cname:
        write_file(out / "CNAME", str(cname) + "\n")

    pages = [c for c in book.chapters if c.is_page()]
    for ch in pages:
        fp = norm_join(book.src_dir, ch.path)
        try:
            text = fp.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            text = fp.read_text(errors="replace")
        text = preprocess_content(book, ch, text)
        mt = TITLE_RE.search(text)
        if mt:
            ch.page_title_override = mt.group(1).strip()
            text = TITLE_RE.sub("", text)
        ch.content = text
        ch.main_html, ch.headings, _ = render_markdown_to_html(text, smart=smart)

    first_page = pages[0] if pages else None
    for idx, ch in enumerate(pages):
        prev_ch = pages[idx-1] if idx > 0 else None
        next_ch = pages[idx+1] if idx + 1 < len(pages) else None
        html_text = render_page(book, ch, ch.main_html, ch.href, page_title(book, ch), prev_ch, next_ch,
                                search_enabled, additional_css, additional_js, mathjax)
        fs = out / Path(ch.href.split("#", 1)[0])
        write_file(fs, html_text)
        if ch is first_page and ch.href != "index.html":
            write_file(out / "index.html", html_text)

    # Default or custom 404.
    input404 = html_cfg.get("input-404")
    if input404:
        p = norm_join(book.src_dir, str(input404))
        if p.exists():
            txt = preprocess_content(book, Chapter(path=str(input404)), p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            main, _, _ = render_markdown_to_html(txt, smart=smart)
            href = chapter_href(str(input404))
            write_file(out / Path(href), render_page(book, None, main, href, (book.title or ""), None, None,
                                                     search_enabled, additional_css, additional_js, mathjax))
    else:
        main404, _, _ = render_markdown_to_html("# Document not found (404)\n\nThis URL is invalid, sorry. Please use the navigation bar or search to continue.\n", smart=smart)
        t404 = f"Page not found - {book.title}" if book.title else "Page not found"
        base = str(html_cfg.get("site-url", "") or "")
        write_file(out / "404.html", render_page(book, None, main404, "404.html", t404, None, None,
                                                  search_enabled, additional_css, additional_js, mathjax, base_href=base))

    # Print page.
    print_parts: List[str] = []
    for i, ch in enumerate(pages):
        if i:
            print_parts.append('<div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div>')
        print_parts.append(ch.main_html)
    write_file(out / "print.html", render_page(book, None, "".join(print_parts), "print.html", book.title or "", None, None,
                                               search_enabled, additional_css, additional_js, mathjax))

    write_file(out / "toc.html", render_toc_html(book, search_enabled, additional_css))
    write_file(out / "toc.js", render_toc_js(book))
    if search_enabled:
        write_file(out / "searchindex.js", render_search_index(book, pages))

    redirs = get_in(book.cfg, ["output", "html", "redirect"], {})
    if isinstance(redirs, dict):
        for src, target in redirs.items():
            dest_rel = str(src).lstrip("/")
            write_file(out / dest_rel, render_redirect(str(target)))

    if bool(html_cfg.get("hash-files", False)):
        apply_hashes(out)


def render_markdown_backend(book: Book, out: Path) -> None:
    if out.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for ch in book.chapters:
        if not ch.path:
            continue
        src = norm_join(book.src_dir, ch.path)
        if not src.exists():
            continue
        txt = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        txt = preprocess_content(book, ch, txt)
        dest = out / Path(ch.path)
        write_file(dest, txt)


def run_external_backend(book: Book, name: str) -> None:
    cfg = get_in(book.cfg, ["output", name], {})
    optional = bool(cfg.get("optional", False)) if isinstance(cfg, dict) else False
    command = str(cfg.get("command", f"mdbook-{name}") if isinstance(cfg, dict) else f"mdbook-{name}")
    log("INFO", "mdbook_driver::builtin_renderers", f'Invoking the "{name}" renderer')
    exe = command.split()[0]
    if shutil.which(exe) is None:
        if optional:
            log("WARN", "mdbook_driver::builtin_renderers", f"The command `{exe}` for backend `{name}` was not found, but was marked as optional.")
        else:
            log("ERROR", "mdbook_driver::builtin_renderers", f"The command `{exe}` wasn't found, is the \"{name}\" backend installed? If you want to ignore this error when the \"{name}\" backend is not installed, set `optional = true` in the `[output.{name}]` section of the book.toml configuration file.")
            log_error("Rendering failed", ["Unable to start the backend", "No such file or directory (os error 2)"])
        return
    # For custom commands, feed a small JSON-ish payload compatible enough for
    # toy backends, but do not fail mdBook if it exits successfully.
    try:
        subprocess.run(command, shell=True, input="{}", text=True, cwd=str(book.root), check=False)
    except Exception as e:
        if not optional:
            log_error("Rendering failed", [str(e)])


def build_book(root_arg: str = ".", dest_dir: Optional[str] = None, open_after: bool = False) -> Path:
    book = load_book(root_arg, create=True, check_missing=True)
    renderers = output_renderers(book.cfg)
    log("INFO", "mdbook_driver::mdbook", "Book building has started")
    warn_index_collisions(book)
    final_html_out: Optional[Path] = None
    for name in renderers:
        log("INFO", "mdbook_driver::mdbook", f"Running the {name} backend")
        out = renderer_out_dir(book, name, dest_dir, renderers)
        if name == "html":
            render_html_backend(book, out)
            final_html_out = out
            log("INFO", "mdbook_html::html_handlebars::hbs_renderer", f"HTML book written to `{out}`")
        elif name == "markdown":
            render_markdown_backend(book, out)
        else:
            run_external_backend(book, name)
    if open_after:
        log("INFO", "mdbook", "Opening web browser")
    if final_html_out is not None:
        return final_html_out
    # If there is no html renderer, return the generic build dir.
    bd = Path(dest_dir if dest_dir is not None else book.build_dir_name())
    if not bd.is_absolute():
        bd = book.root / bd
    return bd
